original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

scope_change_reason: The broad pair-of-calls card is narrowed to an explicit s>=2 shared-bilinear-sum interface: accumulate the common products in one required dirty output, then perform one two-wave compensation. The construction is checked as a local reversible map and is not presented as a selected supplier placement.

candidate_scope_triage.reason: Discussion #1587s unpaid-coordinate investigation and open coverage threshold PR #1348 cover the changed-coverage premise.
Discussion #1516 and open budget screens PR #1791/#1888 cover this route.
Active adjacent work covers one common product (s=1); the experiment changes the object to s>=2 common terms and coalesces their boundary compensation.

actual_scope: For q>=2 arbitrary-dirty output accumulators with a required dirty anchor A0, realize A_i_out=A_i_in+sum_{j=1}^s x_j*y_j+u_i*v_i for s>=2 using s+q product-add children and 2(q-1) width-w row additions; compare with independent evaluation and repeated one-term dirty-anchor fanout.
bottleneck_link: The persistent anchor avoids recomputing each shared bilinear term in every output and carries the entire shared sum across s consecutive child calls. It reduces q(s+1) product children to s+q, and coalesces 2s(q-1) one-term compensation additions into 2(q-1).
stop_rule: Stop after deriving the exact forward and inverse schedules, checking the symbolic identity for 2<=q<=5 and 1<=s<=4, exhausting all dirty/input states for q=s=2 over F2 and F3, validating the full child/addition formulas, and computing the eight-block rank-only ceiling screen. Do not infer a selected-word instance or supplier admission without a source-incidence mapping.
evidence: The reversible schedule is exact for arbitrary dirty outputs and read-only sources. Exhaustive q=s=2 replay covers 60,073 states across F2 and F3; symbolic checks cover the stated q,s rectangle. For q=3,s=3,w=1, independent evaluation uses 12 children, the aggregate anchor uses 6 children plus 4 row additions, and repeating the one-term fanout uses 12 row additions. Eight hypothetical blocks save 48 rank-one children and 32 width-one additions; even waiving additions, the selected fixed-word ceiling gain is only 0.905971%.
author: Cinna Davis, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents.
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance in overlap exploration, construction derivation, exact symbolic and finite-state verification, cost accounting, and package writing. No subagents were used.

open_questions.why_it_matters: The local schedule lowers child and compensation counts, but a source-level incidence match is needed before it can change a paid recursive profile.
